quotes.text: Not yet, not thinking about quitting just yet. It crosses your mind. You know, you're getting old. You know my old friend BB King passed away. And I know BB was doing shows, he was singing the same songs maybe three or four times. Well, my memory's not as good as it was when I was young some years ago. I used to be able to listen to a song, those lyrics maybe once and recall it. But now I have to keep it in my mind more. Sometimes in the studio, I have to read the lyrics while I'm recording. So, retirement comes to your mind at times, though life goes on. I think about maybe relaxing a bit more, letting those young people come through and carry it on.

I see young players coming up, you know, young enough to be my grandchildren but they're playing guitars! And I think, 'How can they do that? How come I wasn't that good at that age?!' I listen to them young guys and I think, 'if they're good enough, let's get them out there, give them that chance. Eric Clapton came to New York a while back. I said to him 'let's get out and see this young guy. Let's see this one, this guy can play some!' Eric listened, he was amazed. 'Where did you find him?' he asked. I replied: 'I didn't find him, I don't think I found him. He found me!' We all laughed.

Every day I just pinch myself or slap myself that I'm still here, that I'm still alive. I never thought I'd still be here, still be around now making music, doing this! I still remember being on the farm as a nine or ten-year-old. We'd no running water till I was around fourteen, not wanting to go to school, just wanting to play around. Being here as a musician now, I just never even dreamed of that!
You went to church in those days. Listened to those great singers there. We'd work the farm six days a week then go to church on Sunday, listen to the gospel.

I didn't start with no Diddley Bo. My first guitar was a rubber band on nails attached to my mother's house wall. And a piece of wire that I could move my fingers on to make sounds. So she could hear me play. I remember thinking then, 'I can manage this!' Some people made that story about me and a Diddley Bo. But it was never my thing. I got a guitar and I started to learn real fast. I listened to Arthur Cruddup, Robert Johnson, and those guys. I worked real hard, always listening and learning.
I left Louisiana in around 1957. I mostly lied to get away. I lied to my mother.
